SOC 2 / ISO evidence for log collection
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Mark Davenport: Doing well, thanks. We'll get straight to it, curious about audit logs and admin activity — what you capture and how we can export to our SIEM.

00:14 Priya Kapoor: Great. We'll cover capture, retention, export options, and encryption. Quick note, we'll reference our SOC 2 documentation at the end. Some of the product names might get fuzzy in transcription, apologies for that.
00:28 Leah Kim: 45 minutes total, is that right? Good. We have a few constraints — logs must be retained for 7 years for some regulated lines, and anything PII has to be redacted or excluded.

00:40 Priya Kapoor: Understood. Quick overview: Redwood's audit log plane captures admin actions (create/delete/update on models, routes, keys), authentication events (SSO/SAML sign-ins, failures), API usage metadata (request id, model, tokens, latency), and system events (deploys, autoscale, failures).
01:05 Evan Ross: Do you capture the request payloads, like prompt text? That's a big one for us.

01:12 Jordan Blake: Good question. For hosted customers by default we capture metadata and a hashed or redacted prompt depending on settings. For Dedicated/Private we can configure full payload capture but it needs to be part of the contract — also note PII handling and data residency there.
01:35 Sophia Zhang: So for Sunrise Insurance, we can't keep raw prompts for regulated workflows. We need an option to strip or redact prompts before stored in logs. Is that supported?

01:44 Priya Kapoor: Yes. We have log filters and pre-ingest processors. You can configure redact rules or disable payload capture and only log the request id and sampling hashes. We'll show a sample later.
02:05 Mark Davenport: What about admin attribution — if someone makes a change through the API using a service account, do you store who performed the action and from where?

02:15 Priya Kapoor: We capture actor identity (SSO username or service account id), IP address, user agent, timestamp, and the before/after diff for config objects. On Private you'd get more detail in the on-prem logs as well.
02:40 Leah Kim: Can those logs be exported to our Splunk stack? We prefer S3 backups and Splunk ingestion via syslog forwarder.

02:48 Priya Kapoor: Yes, export options include push to customer S3 buckets, syslog (TCP/UDP), and a pull-style API for log streaming. For high-volume customers we recommend S3 + Lambda/Splunk ingestion or Kinesis.
03:05 Evan Ross: Is S3 export encrypted with our KMS key? We need CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys).

03:12 Jordan Blake: For Dedicated and Private, yes you can use your AWS KMS keys (CMEK). For hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise accounts — we'll include the details in the compliance pack.
03:28 Sophia Zhang: Any HSM integration for key rotation audits? We need the audit that shows when keys were rotated and by whom.

03:34 Priya Kapoor: We have key rotation logs integrated into audit trails; for HSM/KMS-based keys you get rotation metadata and we surface when rotation happened and the principal that initiated it, provided that's performed through the control plane.
03:50 Mark Davenport: Retention — can we set different retention for different log types? For example, authentication events 7 years, request metadata 1 year, full payloads 30 days.

04:02 Priya Kapoor: Yes, retention policies are per-log-type. Policies can be configured in the Console or via the API and enforced per-tenant. We also support legal hold which marks logs to be immutable until released.
04:20 Leah Kim: Is immutability guaranteed for hosted accounts? We're concerned about tamper evidence for audit purposes.

04:27 Jordan Blake: For hosted we provide append-only storage + tamper-evident digests (hash chains). For regulatory evidence we can provide attestations and include those digests in the SOC 2 reporting. For Dedicated/Private, you can enforce immutability at the storage layer (S3 Object Lock).
04:49 Evan Ross: How granular are the RBAC controls for viewing logs? We don't want all engineers seeing admin diffs.

04:57 Priya Kapoor: RBAC is role-based and can be mapped to SAML groups. You can define roles that allow read-only access to metadata but restrict access to payloads or diffs. We support attribute-based rules too — e.g., only members of the security group can view unredacted payloads.
05:18 Sophia Zhang: What about API keys? If an admin creates an API key, do you capture the key material in logs?
05:24 Priya Kapoor: We never log secret material. We capture creation event, the key id, who created it, and rotation/deletion events, but not the secret itself.
05:34 Mark Davenport: For SOC 2 evidence, how do you provide historical access — like 'show me who changed RBAC in last 6 months' with proof?
05:42 Jordan Blake: We can export relevant audit slices with cryptographic digests and include supporting artifacts. We'll include the runbook we use for SOC 2 evidence in the packet we send.
06:00 Leah Kim: Ok, show us an example of a log entry format please — the fields you're recording.

06:08 Priya Kapoor: Sure — example: timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, before_state (optional), after_state (optional), request_id, ip_address, user_agent, service_node, latency_ms, and a schema version. We'll send a full CSV/JSON schema.
06:40 Evan Ross: If we use S3 export, what's the delivery frequency? Near real-time? Batch?

06:46 Priya Kapoor: We offer near-real-time streaming to Kinesis or syslog; S3 exports are batched hourly or daily depending on volume. For SIEM ingestion many customers use streaming to Kinesis or Pub/Sub and then forward into Splunk.
07:00 Mark Davenport: We need the ability to retain logs in specific regions — e.g., eu-west-1 for EU customers. Is region pinning supported?

07:07 Jordan Blake: Yes, region-level log residency is supported for Dedicated and for hosted enterprise customers. We'll need to set that up in account config; otherwise logs default to the region of the workload.
07:20 Leah Kim: How about exporting data for eDiscovery — can we search across tenants? We need cross-tenant search for merged incidents.

07:28 Priya Kapoor: Cross-tenant search is restricted for security; we can do cross-account export into a central analytics bucket if you need aggregated search, but you need appropriate permissions. We'll advise on best practice and least privilege patterns.
07:44 Sophia Zhang: Any caveats on performance? If we enable full payload logging and high retention, will it affect latency?

07:51 Priya Kapoor: Logging is asynchronous and designed to avoid adding tail latency. However, extreme synchronous payload capture in the request path can add a few ms — we generally recommend async capture with sampling for high-volume endpoints.
08:07 Evan Ross: Can we configure sampling rules? For example, sample 1% of prompts for analysis and full logs for flagged users.
08:14 Priya Kapoor: Yes, sampling rules by route, model, user, or custom attributes are supported. You can also set conditional capture e.g., when output triggers a safety rule.
08:30 Mark Davenport: About export security — does the S3 export support VPC endpoints and S3 bucket policies so data never crosses public internet?
08:38 Jordan Blake: Absolutely. We support VPC endpoints, S3 Block Public Access, bucket policies, and we can use VPC peering for Dedicated customers so the export never transits the public internet.
08:52 Leah Kim: Is there an audit trail of the exports themselves? Who requested exports and when?
08:57 Priya Kapoor: Yes, export operations are logged as admin events with full attribution and export hashes so you can prove the exported dataset integrity.
09:10 Sophia Zhang: Do you include a checksum or signature on exported batches for tamper evidence?
09:15 Priya Kapoor: We include SHA-256 signatures and an index file containing chunk-level digests. For enterprise we can provide an audit bundle with the signature chain.
09:31 Evan Ross: For long retention like 7 years, any pricing caveats? Storage costs add up. We need a cost estimate.
09:38 Jordan Blake: We'll include retention pricing tiers in the packet. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and sample rates to reduce storage of payloads where appropriate.
09:50 Mark Davenport: How do you handle legal hold if a litigation hold is placed?
09:55 Priya Kapoor: We support legal hold flags that prevent deletion of logs regardless of retention policy. Holds are themselves auditable events and require designated roles to set/release.
10:12 Leah Kim: One concern — we want to ensure SSO mapping to users is consistent. If someone authenticates via multiple identity providers, how do you map them in logs?
10:20 Priya Kapoor: We recommend canonical identifiers (e.g., corporate email) and support mapping rules in the identity configuration. We store both raw assertion and canonical_uid where possible.
10:33 Sophia Zhang: Ok show us the specific fields again with an example line — and include a redaction example.

10:40 Priya Kapoor: Example log line — 2026-03-10T15:01:02Z, tenant:sunrise, actor:mark.d@sunrise, action:update_route, resource:route-123, before:{timeout:30}, after:{timeout:45}, request_id:rq_abc123, ip:1.2.3.4, ua:curl/7.68, node:node-4, latency_ms:12. Redacted example replaces prompt with [REDACTED] or stores a hash prompt_sha256. We'll attach sample files.
11:05 Mark Davenport: For compliance we need to see a sample of those logs with masked data to validate ingestion mapping to our SIEM — can you provide?
11:11 Jordan Blake: Yes, Priya will share a redacted sample CSV/JSON, plus mapping guide for Splunk.
